title: Analysis: Meridian's Vireo deal is a bet on owning the multi-cloud control plane
author: Hannah Price
text:
Meridian Cloud's agreement to acquire Vireo Analytics for $1.2 billion looks expensive on paper, but analysts say the hyperscaler is paying for position rather than for sales.

Observability tools sit in an unusual spot: they see every workload a customer runs, regardless of which cloud it lives on. Owning that view gives Meridian data on how enterprises split spending across providers, and a natural place to recommend moving workloads home.

"This is a control-plane play," said Hana Lindqvist, an infrastructure analyst at Brightwater Research. "Whoever owns the dashboard influences where the next dollar of compute goes."

The deal also follows months of speculation. Market Pulse Daily reported in September that the two companies were in talks, and several Vireo customers said this week that they would watch closely whether multi-cloud support survives the integration.

Rival platforms are unlikely to welcome the move. At least two competing providers have previously restricted the telemetry that third-party monitoring tools can collect, and similar friction could follow once Vireo belongs to a competitor.

For Meridian, the risk is that customers who chose Vireo precisely because it was neutral start looking elsewhere. Retaining them will matter more than the headline price.
